title: `ia host` applies the generated agents, skills and `@hook` groups through the one projection writer, and its receipt lists them
summary: @inventarch/cli: `ia host <claude|codex>` and `ia init --host` render the position packet together with the files and hooks generated from the workspace's authored records, computed once, and apply exactly that set through the one projection writer: for claude one .claude/agents/<name>.md per authored `@agent-profile` and one .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per authored `@playbook`, each with the packet marker, and one hook group per authored `@hook` in .claude/settings.local.json; for codex one .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per playbook, every profile and hook reported as not taken. One apply retires a 1.x steward guard, then registers or removes the hook groups against the payload `ia host` materializes and verifies, then writes the files, then the receipt. A record renamed or deleted takes its obsolete agent file, skill or group away on the next apply; unrelated settings keys and groups and unmarked files are kept; a second apply changes no file, setting or state and writes the same receipt rows. `ia project`, the install, update and remove refresh and a migration keep the groups an earlier `ia host` registration owns in step with the records, against the payload that registration recorded; with no registration they register none and list each declared hook as not taken. The receipt gains generated (record identity, word, path and SHA-256 of each generated file), definitions (each authored `@operation` with its handler and validator ids copied as authored and never resolved or run, and each `@harness` with the agents, skills and hooks it registers), hooks (each owned group by `@hook` identity, the tools the hook declares and the group's SHA-256) and unsupported (each authored record the host does not take, with the reason); removed also lists the generated files an apply deleted; a receipt without these sections still reads. The plans of `ia host` and `ia project` list each hook group's action (create, update, unchanged or remove) and each record not taken. A generation refusal keeps its own code and names ia validate. `ia doctor` adds a row for each owned hook group that is missing (deleted by hand) or modified (changed or duplicated): a fail whose remedy is `ia host claude --remove --apply`, after which `ia host claude --apply` registers the workspace's hooks again, since apply never puts back a group the user took away; a guard group naming --hook that no registration owns is a warning, left in place; and an outdated row when the generated rows differ from the receipt's, a receipt written before generation included. @inventarch/distribution: the ./projection subpath exports GENERATED_PATHS and projectionOwnable(host, path). The planner owns generated files at .claude/agents/<name>.md, .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md through the same ia.host-projection-state.v1 state: an owned one no render writes any more is removed, an unmarked or hand-edited file at a generated path is refused and never overwritten or removed, a generated agent is refused (IA-DIST-PATH-UNSAFE) where .claude/agents is a link, and a generated agent at the path of an owned 1.x steward file replaces it as one update, never an update and a remove of the same path. @inventarch/steward-hook: projection protection reads a state that lists generated skills and protects them, as it protects generated agents. Limits: ownership stays in the projection and hook ownership states, never the receipt; Codex agents and hooks remain unsupported; a 2.0.0 CLI cannot plan a workspace this release applied a generated set to until the registration is removed (see the state-evolution note).
